title: Temporal Dynamics-Aware Adversarial Attacks on Discrete-Time Dynamic Graph Models

problem.claim: The work addresses adversarial attacks against representation learners for discrete-time dynamic graphs while preserving the graphs' temporal dynamics.

gap.claim: The robustness of dynamic-graph representation learners to adversarial attacks is highly understudied.

contributions.claim: A Temporal Dynamics-Aware Perturbation constraint restricts perturbations at each time step to a small fraction of the graph changes since the previous time step.
A theoretically motivated Projected Gradient Descent approach finds effective perturbations for dynamic graphs under the TDAP constraint.
The approach is extended to an online setting with real-time graph availability and is used to evade neural anomaly-detection approaches.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a novel adversarial attack for discrete-time dynamic graph models and motivate a novel TDAP constraint.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On dynamic link prediction and node classification, the approach is reported to be up to 4x more effective than baseline attack methods.
In the online setting, the approach is reported to achieve up to 5x superior performance over baselines.
The approach is reported to successfully evade state-of-the-art neural anomaly-detection methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Real-world graphs evolve over time, and deep architectures learn node representations from graph structure and dynamics.
The robustness of dynamic-graph representation learners under adversarial attacks is understudied.
The work introduces dynamics-preserving graph-sequence attacks, the TDAP constraint, and a projected-gradient method operating under that constraint.
Experiments on dynamic link prediction and node classification report up to 4x greater attack effectiveness than baselines.
An online real-time setting reports up to 5x superior performance over baselines and successful evasion of neural anomaly detectors.

source_observation.claim: Perturbations are constrained relative to the number of graph changes between consecutive time steps.

interpretation.claim: Adversarial evaluation of dynamic systems can preserve plausible temporal evolution by budgeting perturbations against natural temporal change.

application.claim: Use temporal-change-aware perturbation budgets when testing robustness of models that consume evolving graph sequences.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this constraint preserves all relevant real-world temporal properties or applies beyond the studied dynamic-graph setting.

source_observation.claim: The reported attack is evaluated on dynamic link prediction, node classification, online graphs, and neural anomaly detection.

interpretation.claim: Robustness assessment should consider multiple downstream tasks and deployment conditions for dynamic-graph representation learners.

application.claim: Evaluate dynamic-graph robustness across offline prediction, classification, online arrival, and anomaly-detection scenarios where relevant.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the datasets, model families, baseline definitions, or generalizability of the reported results.

unknowns: Datasets, graph sizes, and temporal resolutions are not specified.
Compared representation learners, baseline methods, and evaluation metrics are not specified.
The perturbation budget and optimization details are not specified.
The meaning of 'up to' 4x and 5x and the statistical variability of results are not specified.
Theoretical guarantees and limitations are not specified.
